what: apr vs llama.cpp, qwen2.5-coder-7b-instruct Q4_K_M, one client both sides
instrument: apr test llm bench (GH-876 Milestone 2) — the SAME OpenAI client, prompts and clock drives both servers
protocol: scripts/llama_pin.toml [protocol.http]: profile medium (128 in/128 out), warmup 15s, 3 x 30s, cooldown 10s, concurrency 1, streaming

mechanism_engaged.note: Neither side is labelled by intent. Each is a line the runtime printed.
mechanism_engaged.llamacpp: load_tensors: offloaded 29/29 layers to GPU; device CUDA0 (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090)
mechanism_engaged.apr: Enabling optimized CUDA acceleration (PAR-111) ... CUDA optimized model ready
mechanism_engaged.isolation: measured SEQUENTIALLY; GPU returned to ~650 MiB between lanes, so neither held VRAM while the other ran

headline: Three runtimes, one client. llama.cpp 158.9 decode; apr built --features cuda 103.3 (0.650x); apr AS PUBLISHED 15.7 (0.099x) with 7.5s to first token. The cuda feature is worth 6.6x on decode and 211x on prefill, and cargo install does not enable it.
corrects: The 11.8 tok/s figure reported on 2026-08-24 was an END-TO-END rate that included ~9.7s of model load. apr's actual decode rate here is 103.3 tok/s — 2.6x the ~40 tok/s 7B reference in CLAUDE.md, not below it. The parity gap is real but it is against llama.cpp's 158.9, not against apr's history.

published_artifact.identity: apr 0.64.0 (v0.64.0+no-git) at ~/.cargo/bin/apr — a cargo install of the published crate
published_artifact.control_probe: a string known absent also returns 0, so the probe discriminates
published_artifact.vram_while_serving_with_--gpu: 0 MiB — nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps lists no apr process
published_artifact.verdict: --gpu is ACCEPTED AND IGNORED; the run completes and returns a plausible number

root_cause.finding: apr materializes a SECOND, dequantized copy of every weight for prefill; llama.cpp does not.
root_cause.decisive_experiment: toggling FP8_PREFILL moved VRAM in the direction OPPOSITE to intuition

vram_by_prefill_format.prediction: one extra byte per weight over ~7.6B params

vram_scaling.fit: VRAM = 3.25 * file - 0.45 GiB (no meaningful fixed term)

ruled_out: KV cache and context length: 512 and 4096 both give 14030 MiB, byte-identical
dequantization on upload: load_quantized_weights_with_type uploads RAW quantized bytes
indexed weights: build_indexed_weights stores POINTERS, not copies

explains.#2693 prefill 3.64x: prefill reads 1 B/elem vs llama.cpp's Q4_K 0.5625 -- a 1.78x bandwidth floor no kernel tuning gets below while the copy exists

root_cause.fix: a Q4_K-direct prefill GEMM (dequantize per tile in shared memory) and drop the materialized copy: VRAM 3.25x -> ~1.05x, prefill bandwidth 1.78x -> 1.0x, decode untouched
root_cause.note: FP8 prefill is a deliberate tradeoff that made the second copy CHEAPER (TTFT 46.4 -> 35.5 ms, 1.31x). It did not question the second copy.
root_cause.CORRECTION: The '1.78x prefill bandwidth floor' stated in root_cause.explains is FALSIFIED. FP8_PREFILL=0 doubles the weight bytes read (1 -> 2 B/elem) and moves TTFT by 2% (35.4 -> 36.1 ms). Prefill is NOT weight-bandwidth-bound, so removing the second copy does not speed it up on its own. The VRAM finding is unaffected -- it was measured independently.

prefill_decomposition.method: TTFT vs prompt length, 3 runs per point, all spreads < 1 ms

two_problems.fixed_cost: 23.1 vs 7.8 ms = 3.0x; 71% of apr's TTFT at the 102-token gate workload is paid before the first prompt token is looked at
two_problems.per_token_cost: 0.0916 vs 0.0080 ms = 11.4x; this is why the ratio WORSENS with prompt length (3.0x -> 4.8x)

prefill_decomposition.gate_implication: the single medium-profile number understates the gap for long prompts; the gate should also measure `long`

prefill_graph_blocked: PREFILL_GRAPH=1 capture fails with CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY at S=126 because apr already holds 14030 MiB of a 24 GiB card. The second weight copy blocks the CUDA graph path from being evaluated at all -- a real reason to remove it, and a different one from the falsified bandwidth argument.
